4.speaker: Petr Vectern
4.text: "I agree. This really has no importance for the new Constitution. Also, Soll was a hero for many Sords, whether we like it or not."

5.speaker: Player
5.text: "Yes, he is a hero for Sordland."

6.speaker: Player
6.text: "Regardless of him, I see no problem with having a special title for great heroes."

7.speaker: Petr Vectern
7.text: "Even Mr. Clavin and our party's reformist wing has no problems with the current law. USP would fully support that decision. I guess we could also persuade Mr. Kibener somehow."

8.speaker: Lucian Galade
8.text: "We'll never be able to get PFJP to work with us. But if you can get Kesaro Kibener to work with you on this, our only remaining problem would be uniting our own party."

9.speaker: Petr Vectern
9.text: "You would be opening their way into the parliament in the future if you were to decrease the threshold. It is important that you realize this."

16.speaker: Player
16.text: "No, I think we should respect this law."

18.speaker: Petr Vectern
18.text: "Oh, so you want to use the same privilege after all."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "Every President should gain that title after their term."

20.speaker: Lucian Galade
20.text: "Some reformists suggested that the Assembly should nominate the ministers before the President approves them."

22.speaker: Petr Vectern
22.text: "I think some of the reformists really want to try him for his crimes during his terms. This law really has symbolic importance for both them and the Sollists."

23.speaker: Player
23.text: "Do you think they can be persuaded?"

24.speaker: Petr Vectern
24.text: "That's why only Tarquin Soll has it. He gave it to himself right after his military coup. This law is basically made to save the Colonel."

25.speaker: Lucian Galade
25.text: "According to the Constitution, the Member of Honor not only has legal immunity but the state also covers most of their expenses as well as providing security at all times. It can only be given to someone by an absolute majority vote in the Assembly and the approval of the President."

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: Lucian couldn't hide the surprised look on his face.

27.speaker: Player
27.text: "We should open their way and unite the left."

28.speaker: Lucian Galade
28.text: "And the last one is the question about Soll's legacy. Basically his *Member of Honor* law. It gave him absolute immunity even when he's retired. He is a permanent member of the Assembly as well, but luckily he doesn't really attend anymore."

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "After pushing aggressive changes, I may need the same immunity."

31.speaker: Petr Vectern
31.text: "But it would be tougher to persuade the judges with this. Mrs. Edmonds and Mr. Garaci may not want to cooperate with you if they believe you're going to get rid of them afterwards."

32.speaker: Lucian Galade
32.text: "I'm afraid it would be tough to bribe the Old Guards. Chief Justice Hawker will do their best to undermine us. But maybe we can get to Heron Garaci."

33.speaker: Petr Vectern
33.text: "Albin Clavin and his reformist wing will be completely against you. He already responded negatively in the committee meetings. I think he would be tough to break."

35.speaker: Lucian Galade
35.text: "That's very bold, sir. But I like it."

36.speaker: Petr Vectern
36.text: "That might be the best thing to do for now. If we agitate the Court further, we might lose our chances with Mrs. Edmonds as well."

37.speaker: Petr Vectern
37.text: "However, the conservatives may be persuaded easier. The influence of Soll is still living strong in the party. They might follow you if they respect you as a strong leader."

38.speaker: Player
38.text: "Maybe we shouldn't make the Supreme Court our enemies just yet."

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "I will instead give the President the ability to replace Judges as necessary."

41.speaker: Player
41.text: "We should crush the Old Guards to clear ways for further reforms."

42.speaker: Petr Vectern
42.text: "If we can remove their immunity or define an impeachment process, we could clean the Court from Orso and his gang."

43.speaker: Lucian Galade
43.text: "That is a fair concern. We'll need to sway some of their members to succeed after all."

44.speaker: Petr Vectern
44.text: "Sure. You'll have some time before we start writing the final proposal together."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: "I may need to think a bit longer about this."

46.speaker: Petr Vectern
46.text: "So we need as many of the conservatives to support us. And there is one key person who can help us get their support."

47.speaker: Lucian Galade
47.text: "It's the question about the immunity of the Judges. While the Anti-Old Guard sentiment is increasing, there are talks that taking away their immunity would give us authority over judiciary."

48.speaker: Petr Vectern
48.text: "And there is one key person who can help us get their support."

49.speaker: Lucian Galade
49.text: "Now I'll move unto the 8th Section. We are reaching the end."

50.speaker: Petr Vectern
50.text: "And there is another key person who can help us get their support."

51.speaker: Lucian Galade
51.text: "We can also try to "persuade" the centrists of the Court. I think we might get Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin with a bribe. The toughest will be Mrs. Edmonds."

52.speaker: Lucian Galade
52.text: "We will leave it to the President to decide."

53.speaker: Petr Vectern
53.text: "Hey, if people keep electing one person, that means they really are content. The masses are scared of change."

54.speaker: Petr Vectern
54.text: "Yes, we'll need to talk to Judge Edmonds. If we can get to her and Judge Garaci, we might be able to get enough votes. They have major influence."

55.speaker: Player
55.text: "A decrease is out of the question."

59.speaker: Lucian Galade
59.text: "For now I'll move onto the next one: Term Limits.

60.speaker: Lucian Galade
60.text: "Yes. Tarquin Soll governed for twenty years. It seems his magic is slowly vanishing from the minds of the people, for they believe term limits are necessary."

61.speaker: Lucian Galade
61.text: "I agree, we could keep that in."

62.speaker: Lucian Galade
62.text: "According to the Constitution, Nia Morgna is a member of the Supreme Court, which means we already have one vote against this. I know two of the judges who are with her, as well."

63.speaker: Petr Vectern
63.text: "Unlikely to have 100% vote to pass. But I hear you."

65.speaker: Petr Vectern
65.text: "That would be enough to hold him accountable for his actions but why would you want to keep such the title then?"

67.speaker: Player
67.text: "We could keep the title but take away the immunity clause."

68.speaker: Petr Vectern
68.text: "We will also need to get more votes from the conservative judges. I believe Heron Garaci might be the weakest link of the Old Guards. He can help us get the 6 votes needed."

69.speaker: Petr Vectern
69.text: "We could try to balance it with the reformists and make it dependent on an enabling act from the Assembly. Sure, it would make the whole process longer but as long as we have a majority, nothing really changes."

70.speaker: Player
70.text: "Yes, we can make it dependent on enabling acts."

71.speaker: Lucian Galade
71.text: "Mr. Ricter will probably demand that we remove them completely. I doubt that this would be enough to get him to sit down with us."

72.speaker: Player
72.text: "I don't think presidential decrees need any reforms."

73.speaker: Lucian Galade
73.text: "Me neither. I think it's important that the President can act quickly on matters of national importance."

74.speaker: Petr Vectern
74.text: "We'll need to reach out to Judge Edmonds and her centrist wing. We can get three votes from them. They don't seem to be in the pocket of the Old Guard and they are definitely not reformists."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: "I don't aim to leave any time soon. We keep the unlimited terms."

77.speaker: Petr Vectern
77.text: "I'm sure it's possible. But regardless of my opinion, we *need* to persuade most of them to support us for passing an amendment to the Constitution."

78.speaker: Player
78.text: "We can't allow communists to enter the Assembly."

79.speaker: Petr Vectern
79.text: "The conservatives have around 40 seats. If you can get the unaligned to support us, along with our "loyalists" we'll have enough votes."

80.speaker: Player
80.text: "So, we don't even have a vote in the Court?"

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "Who do you think would be willing to support these changes?"

82.speaker: Player
82.text: "We should strengthen the decrees further, so they have priority over statute law."

83.speaker: Lucian Galade
83.text: "You could technically choose to take no action instead of signing or vetoing it. Without a proper definition of the process, it would be perfectly legal for you to ignore a bill indefinitely."

84.speaker: Lucian Galade
84.text: "That is pretty powerful, indeed. That may scare some of our ministers too if you decide to *rule by decree.*"

86.speaker: Lucian Galade
86.text: "We are at the 6th. This is about the presidential decrees. You already know that the reformists want them to be removed or limited. But I'm guessing you do not want any changes to your already powerful decrees, sir."

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: Lucian continued with the next section.

88.speaker: Lucian Galade
88.text: "Well, we could define a process for the Assembly to override your vetoes with a supermajority. While this limits your veto capabilities, if we do not define a time limit for the President to act on a bill..."

89.speaker: Lucian Galade
89.text: "You'll have some time to think about your decision, sir."

91.speaker: Petr Vectern
91.text: "I agree. If we're going against the reformists anyway, why even bother giving concessions?"

93.speaker: Lucian Galade
93.text: "That said, we should try to reach common ground with NFP and the conservative wing of our party to be able to propose such changes in the Assembly."

94.speaker: Lucian Galade
94.text: "Yes, they are already trying to hit you since they are expecting reforms. But we aim to cooperate with some of the judges to make sure that doesn't happen."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "What if we don't succeed? The Court can have me impeached for this."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "We could add the Assembly in the process but make impeachment possible only with an absolute majority."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "We'll get rid of this law entirely."

99.speaker: Petr Vectern
99.text: "I like the idea. Maybe we could convince some of the reformists with that. But it all depends on the whole changes. It could be better not to change anything."

100.speaker: Player
100.text: "Let's mess with the Court, divide and conquer them."

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: "That's a good idea. That'd make impeachment close to impossible."

102.speaker: Player
102.text: "This is already what we wanted to do."

103.speaker: Player
103.text: "No. We don't need to change the Article about vetoes."

105.speaker: Lucian Galade
105.text: "We could try to make the impeachment process more difficult or entirely get rid of it. A change like this would give you free reign. However, that might be going a little too far."

106.speaker: Lucian Galade
106.text: "This is regarding the appointment of ministers. Currently, the President is free to appoint anyone from the members of the Assembly. Nobody else is involved with the process."

107.speaker: Petr Vectern
107.text: "Decreasing the threshold might mean opening their way into the Assembly."

108.speaker: Lucian Galade
108.text: "That is not bad idea. As long as we are the majority in the Assembly, that does not change too much."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "We could limit the vetoes and package it as a great reform."

111.speaker: Player
111.text: "I agree. We should involve the Assembly more in the process."

112.speaker: Petr Vectern
112.text: "Yes, we'll need the rip some of the sheep Judges out of the herd in the process."

113.speaker: Player
113.text: "Can we pass it through the Supreme Court?"

115.speaker: Player
115.text: "Can we possibly reach a two-thirds majority in the Assembly?"

116.speaker: Player
116.text: "I like the idea. What kind of loopholes do you have in mind?"

118.speaker: Lucian Galade
118.text: "Or better yet, we could change the article according to their demands but establish new loopholes for you to hold your veto powers."

120.speaker: Petr Vectern
120.text: "An increase on the other hand is more complex. NFP could be out of the Assembly but that would mean PFJP's seats would get higher too, if we're left with only two parties in the Assembly."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "We should keep using the threshold to our advantage."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "Don't worry. With these reforms, we will be even more popular."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "We can't just give away our majority like that anyway."

124.speaker: Lucian Galade
124.text: "Well, we can't know these for sure. In the last elections, the Socialist Party and the Worker's Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent. One of them may very well increase their votes in the next years."

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "Let's get into the details of our *reforms.*"

129.speaker: Petr Vectern
129.text: "I'm sure some of the reformists may support that."

130.speaker: Lucian Galade
130.text: "So there is no reason to change this unless you want to sell this to the opposition parties. Sharing the power with the Assembly may make them sympathetic to you. This might be important for the NFP as well."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "They will surely support a just cause for the country and its future."

132.speaker: Lucian Galade
132.text: "We need at least 6 of the 11 judges to vote for the proposal. But Mr. Hawker has enormous influence over the judges."

133.speaker: Lucian Galade
133.text: "They are the biggest obstacle. Even if we pass the Assembly, the Chief Justice will do his best to block our amendments."

135.speaker: Player
135.text: "Did you already work on a plan?"

137.speaker: Lucian Galade
137.text: "We need the majority of our 130 seats in the Assembly to vote in favour. But without NFP's support of 40 votes, we can never surpass the needed 166. Mr. Kibener's full support as well as our party is needed."

139.speaker: Lucian Galade
139.text: "I understand sir. We will address it later in that case."

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: Lucian pulled out a huge dossier from his briefcase.

141.speaker: Player
141.text: "Yea, I am not so sure about this."

143.speaker: Lucian Galade
143.text: "Excellent, and it gives us additional options."

144.speaker: Petr Vectern
144.text: "We should reach out to the judges in secret. Some of them might be willing to break rank to support us."

145.speaker: Player
145.text: "And what good does that do to us?"

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "We need the Court to even pass this change. Why on earth would they support this?"

147.speaker: Petr Vectern
147.text: "But if we keep the same voter base, say a 15% threshold would keep NFP out of the Assembly. Leaving only two parties. Unless, Frens also falls back behind."

148.speaker: Petr Vectern
148.text: "We will be ensuring that the Supreme Court can no longer block constitutional changes."

149.speaker: Petr Vectern
149.text: "Most of them won't. But we already talked about a possible agreement with Isabel which may change things. We could potentially get Heron and the Sollist judges as well."

150.speaker: Lucian Galade
150.text: "Moving on to Section 3. This is about the impeachment process of the President. Currently, in cases of high treason and breaking the Constitution, the Supreme Court may impeach and try the President."

153.speaker: Lucian Galade
153.text: "Most people already find the Supreme Court's absolute authority over constitutional changes dangerous. Look at the situation we currently have, Mr. President. The Judiciary has power over every branch."

154.speaker: Petr Vectern
154.text: "That's why the Old Guard have bargaining chips over us."

155.speaker: Petr Vectern
155.text: "This law is particularly dangerous for you in this case. We will be going against the Old Guard, and if we prove to be successful in the Assembly..."

156.speaker: Petr Vectern
156.text: "Of course, according to the ratio of the party's in government. In our case, it's only us."

157.speaker: Petr Vectern
157.text: "Yes. This will ensure that the Supreme Court will no longer have absolute power over legislation. We can persuade the other parties with this too."

158.speaker: Petr Vectern
158.text: "...They will be looking for anything they can declare unconstitutional to tackle you. All they need is the Supreme Court to impeach you."

159.speaker: Lucian Galade
159.text: "But it will be tough to unite the USP with all the divisive wings that have formed. You must make them follow you loyally."

160.speaker: Lucian Galade
160.text: "I have established nine points parallel to the demands of the reformists. I'll go through each of them and get your input."

162.speaker: Petr Vectern
162.text: "But don't forget that the Socialist party and the Worker's Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."

163.speaker: Player
163.text: "We will do what's necessary to get them in line."

164.speaker: Lucian Galade
164.text: "Some would but it would be possible to pass it, so it doesn't really matter."

165.speaker: Player
165.text: "I don't see anything wrong with it."

166.speaker: Player
166.text: "We did it before for the elections. We can unite it again."

168.speaker: Lucian Galade
168.text: "Now if we are going with this direction, I'll need everybody to focus."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "A pocket veto? Wouldn't the reformist see through that?"

170.speaker: Petr Vectern
170.text: "I know you will. If you can get their support, we'll have enough votes to amend the Constitution, counting we have the support of Mr. Kibener too."

171.speaker: Lucian Galade
171.text: "According to such change, constitutional amendments will still require the two-thirds vote system to be able to propose a change. However, the judiciary will not have the final say in the amendments."

173.speaker: Petr Vectern
173.text: "Yes, but this is a delicate matter. All the party, and I mean, not even Albin wants us to decrease the threshold. They think that... this would destroy our party in the long term."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "We should definitely work to decrease the threshold to some degree."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: "Do you think it would really hurt the party?"

176.speaker: Petr Vectern
176.text: "Two major left parties; the Socialist Party and the Worker's Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."

177.speaker: Petr Vectern
177.text: "Well, we don't. I doubt that any of the judges would support such changes just like that. But they can surely be bribed."

179.speaker: Lucian Galade
179.text: "Not wrong. The ten percent threshold is what that allowed us to control half of the Assembly with around one third of the majority in the elections."

180.speaker: Lucian Galade
180.text: "The fifth section is about our infamous electoral threshold. Most reformists want to lower the threshold as much as possible. We could try working with them but it is simpler to keep the law."

181.speaker: Lucian Galade
181.text: "A decrease would definitely hurt our position in the future. If another party is elected to the Assembly, our projected vote would be closer to the real vote, which is significantly lesser."

182.speaker: Lucian Galade
182.text: "10% seems already too high for many, sir. An increase may bring too much attention on the amendments."

183.speaker: Lucian Galade
183.text: "That's a possibility. It might make the reformists more willing to consider the changes."

185.speaker: Petr Vectern
185.text: "We will definitely need to work with some of the Old Guard aligned judges."

186.speaker: Lucian Galade
186.text: "We'll start with Section 1. Reformists want your absolute veto power to be removed, or at least, limited. We could potentially give them what they want by limiting it. It wouldn't cause problems since we already have the majority in the Assembly."

187.speaker: Petr Vectern
187.text: "This is a point that was unanimously agreed on by all parties. Tarquin Soll established this rule to protect his '29 Constitution. We can break the power of the Old Guards with this."

188.speaker: Lucian Galade
188.text: "I'll move on to the second point then. The new Constitution should remove the Supreme Court out of the constitutional amendment process. Not only popular, it would also strengthen our position against the judiciary."

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: Nia was taken aback by the statement.

190.speaker: Petr Vectern
190.text: "I think we can reach out to Judge Edmonds. And in extension, Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin. They aren't working together with the Old Guards, as far as we know."
